docker_compose_file:
services:
  broker-ingress:
    # Pinned by digest, not by tag, because this container mounts dstack.sock — the
    # same socket that serves EmitEvent and GetKey. Anything holding it can append
    # RTMR3 records and derive any image's keys, so it sits inside the trust
    # boundary the attestation chain rests on, exactly like the controller does.
    # A tag there would let the image be replaced without compose_hash moving.
    #
    # It needs the socket for GetTlsKey (certificate provisioning), so it cannot
    # simply be taken away. What it can be is pinned and reviewed.
    #
    # Re-resolve when upgrading:
    #   docker buildx imagetools inspect dstacktee/dstack-ingress:2.2
    image: dstacktee/dstack-ingress:2.2@sha256:d05a7b343c37c1cca1bba8dbf7e8f3c6d2118158af2d41c455103796db4f67f0
    ports:
      - "443:443"
    environment:
      - CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN=${CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN}
      # No default, deliberately. This container's first act is to point
      # _dstack-app-address.$DOMAIN at itself, which is what moves traffic — so a
      # default of production's hostname means a rehearsal deployment that forgot to
      # set DOMAIN silently takes production's traffic. It nearly happened: a
      # rehearsal ran with DOMAIN unset and was saved only by the broker crashing
      # before it could become healthy. ${VAR:?} fails at render time instead.
      - DOMAIN=${DOMAIN:?set DOMAIN — there is no default, so that a missing value cannot point this deployment at production}
      - TARGET_ENDPOINT=http://0g-serving-provider-broker:3080
      - CERTBOT_EMAIL=${CERTBOT_EMAIL}
      - GATEWAY_DOMAIN=_.${DSTACK_GATEWAY_DOMAIN}
      - SET_CAA=true
      - PORT=443
      - TIMEOUT_CONNECT=10s
      - TIMEOUT_SERVER=900s
    volumes:
      - /var/run/dstack.sock:/var/run/dstack.sock
      - cert-data:/etc/letsencrypt
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      # Nothing fronts the broker until the broker can answer. This container's first
      # act is to point _dstack-app-address.$DOMAIN at this CVM, which is what moves
      # traffic here — so on a fresh deployment it must not run until the model has
      # downloaded, loaded, and the broker behind it reports healthy. Until then the
      # record still names whichever CVM held it before, and that one keeps serving.
      0g-serving-provider-broker:
        condition: service_healthy

  # SGLang server for 0GM-1.0-35B-A3B-0427.
  #
  # Owned by whoever owns the model: the image and every --flag below are theirs, and
  # are taken verbatim. What this deployment changes is only the volume, the host
  # limits and the network aliases — marked where they appear.
  0gm-sglang:
    # Pinned for the same reason as the broker's: this container receives the request
    # after the broker unseals it, so it is inside the confidentiality boundary, and it
    # is the code that enforces --revision below. A tag leaves both unattested.
    #
    # Owned by the model team like the flags are — only the digest is added here.
    image: lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.17-cu129@sha256:220bb1a1a4b38e604ebd33c876a279f6d2519035de141200720417407c9b967d
    container_name: 0gm-sglang
    restart: unless-stopped
    init: true
    ipc: host
    shm_size: 32gb
    runtime: nvidia
    environment:
      NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES: "${NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES:-all}"
      NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES: "compute,utility"
      # Where the weights land. Must point inside the mounted volume below,
      # or every restart re-downloads 72 GB into the container's layer.
      HF_HOME: /dstack/persistent/hf-cache
      # Only needed for private or gated repos; harmless when unset.
      HF_TOKEN: "${HF_TOKEN:-}"
    volumes:
      # Narrowed to the cache HF_HOME names, rather than the whole persistent volume
      # read-write: the download needs somewhere to write and nothing more, and every
      # other container's data lives under that same root.
      - /dstack/persistent/hf-cache:/dstack/persistent/hf-cache
      - /dstack/persistent/benchmark/sglang_0gm_logs:/logs
    command:
      - python3
      - -m
      - sglang.launch_server
      # A HuggingFace repo id, not a local path — this is what makes the
      # download automatic. Swap it to serve a different model.
      - --model-path
      - 0G-AI/0GM-1.0-35B-A3B-0427
      # Pinned, for the reason the broker image is pinned by digest: a repo id names
      # which weights were asked for, not which ones arrive. compose_hash covers this
      # file, so it covers the name — and only a revision makes the name mean one
      # thing. Bump it deliberately when the model moves; HF's current head is
      # reported by https://huggingface.co/api/models/0G-AI/0GM-1.0-35B-A3B-0427
      - --revision
      - 802e58f5c8211f04079bfb5c27fb2c6ab629b686
      - --served-model-name
      - 0GM-1.0-35B-A3B-0427
      - --host
      - 0.0.0.0
      - --port
      - "8000"
      - --tp-size
      - "1"
      - --mem-fraction-static
      - "0.90"
      - --context-length
      - "262144"
      # Both parsers are model-specific. qwen3_coder matches this model's
      # template (<tool_call><function=..><parameter=..>); the similar-looking
      # <tool_call>{"name":..} JSON form would need qwen/hermes instead, and a
      # mismatch fails silently — raw markup is left in the message content.
      - --reasoning-parser
      - qwen3
      - --tool-call-parser
      - qwen3_coder
      # MTP speculative decoding. This model ships the draft weights
      # (mtp_num_hidden_layers=1), so NEXTN is usable.
      - --speculative-algorithm
      - NEXTN
      - --speculative-num-steps
      - "3"
      - --speculative-eagle-topk
      - "1"
      - --speculative-num-draft-tokens
      - "4"
      - --mamba-scheduler-strategy
      - extra_buffer
      - --enable-metrics
      # Without this, prompt caching still works but cached_tokens and
      # cache_read_input_tokens are never populated — indistinguishable from
      # a cache that never hits.
      - --enable-cache-report
    # /health_generate, not /health. Both return 503 while the engine is loading, so
    # either one keeps the broker — and behind it the ingress, and with it the domain —
    # from coming up early. They differ afterwards: with
    # SGLANG_ENABLE_HEALTH_ENDPOINT_GENERATION unset, /health returns 200 on engine
    # state alone, while /health_generate pushes one token through the scheduler and
    # detokenizer. A wedged scheduler is invisible to the first and caught by the
    # second, and the ingress points a public hostname at whatever answers here.
    healthcheck:
      test:
        [
          "CMD-SHELL",
          'python3 -c "import urllib.request;urllib.request.urlopen(''http://localhost:8000/health_generate'',timeout=15)"',
        ]
      interval: 30s
      # Longer than the 15s inside the probe, so a slow generation is reported as a
      # failed check rather than killed by docker before it can answer.
      timeout: 20s
      # Sized for a cold start: 67 GB at 13 MB/s, plus the load. Long is the safe
      # direction — during the start period a failing check does not count, while the
      # first success marks the container healthy immediately, so a generous value
      # costs nothing when things work. Too short is a hard failure instead: the
      # container goes unhealthy mid-download, restart: unless-stopped does not fire
      # on unhealthy, and the broker's depends_on: service_healthy never releases.
      start_period: 90m
      retries: 3
    # Host-level limits and log caps, kept from this deployment's previous block:
    # pinned memory and a large stack are what the CUDA path needs, and without the
    # cap this container's logs grow to whatever the daemon default allows.
    ulimits:
      memlock: -1
      stack: 67108864
    logging:
      driver: json-file
      options:
        max-size: 100m
        max-file: "5"
    networks:
      default:
        aliases:
          # The broker reaches this service by name, and the deployment generator in
          # 0g-serving-broker emits a compose that names "vllm".
          - sglang
          - vllm

  mysql:
    # Pinned: async_job persists RequestBody and ResponseBody as mediumblobs, so this
    # container holds request and response plaintext, not just billing metadata.
    #
    # Re-resolve when upgrading:
    #   docker buildx imagetools inspect mysql:8.0
    image: mysql:8.0@sha256:7dcddc01f13bab2f15cde676d44d01f61fc9f99fe7785e86196dfc07d358ae2b
    # No ports. The dstack gateway accepts every published port at
    # <app-id>-<port>.<gateway-domain>, so publishing this put root:123456 one
    # hostname away from the internet. Only the broker and event containers reach
    # it, and they do that over the compose network.
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      - MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=123456
      - MYSQL_DATABASE=provider
      - MYSQL_USER=provider
      - MYSQL_PASSWORD=provider
    volumes:
      - mysql-data:/var/lib/mysql
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "mysql -uroot -p123456 -e 'USE provider'"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 15
      start_period: 60s
    networks:
      - default

  # Materialises the broker config, because the deploy path has nowhere to put a
  # file: Phala takes a compose file and encrypted environment variables, and
  # nothing else. So the config travels as one base64 variable and is written here.
  #
  # BROKER_CONFIG carries no secrets — it keeps ${PRIVATE_KEY} and
  # ${COINGECKO_API_KEY} as literals and they are substituted below, inside the
  # CVM. That split matters because Phala refuses partial secret updates: had the
  # blob contained the resolved key, every config change would mean handling the
  # provider wallet key again. This way it is set once and never touched, and
  # BROKER_CONFIG stays reviewable and diffable.
  broker-config-init:
    # Pinned, like every other container inside the trust boundary. This one holds
    # PRIVATE_KEY and sits on a network with egress, and dstack re-resolves tags on
    # every boot (app-compose.sh pulls, then prunes unused images), so a tag here means
    # the same compose_hash can run different code against the provider's wallet key.
    #
    # Re-resolve when upgrading:
    #   docker buildx imagetools inspect alpine:3.18
    image: alpine:3.18@sha256:de0eb0b3f2a47ba1eb89389859a9bd88b28e82f5826b6969ad604979713c2d4f
    environment:
      - BROKER_CONFIG=${BROKER_CONFIG:-}
      - PRIVATE_KEY=${PRIVATE_KEY:-}
      - COINGECKO_API_KEY=${COINGECKO_API_KEY:-}
    volumes:
      - broker-config:/config
    command:
      - sh
      - -c
      - |
        set -e
        # First boot only. The controller's PUT /v1/config/core writes this same
        # file and records the change in RTMR3, so rewriting it on every start
        # would silently undo an operator change that is already on-chain — the
        # same guard dstack's own boot script puts on docker-compose.yaml.
        if [ ! -f /config/config.yaml ]; then
          if [ -z "$$BROKER_CONFIG" ]; then
            echo "BROKER_CONFIG is empty and no config exists yet" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          printf '%s' "$$BROKER_CONFIG" | base64 -d \
            | sed -e "s#\$${PRIVATE_KEY}#$$PRIVATE_KEY#" \
                  -e "s#\$${COINGECKO_API_KEY}#$$COINGECKO_API_KEY#" \
            > /config/config.yaml.tmp
          # Rename last, so a container killed mid-write leaves no half-file that
          # the guard above would then accept as complete.
          mv /config/config.yaml.tmp /config/config.yaml
        fi
    restart: "no"


  # Main broker service
  0g-serving-provider-broker:
    # Pinned, because the controller finds this container by exact name and refuses
    # to act on anything else. Without it compose names the container
    # <project>-0g-serving-provider-broker-1 and every upgrade is refused.
    container_name: 0g-serving-provider-broker
    # A digest, never a tag. A tag says which name was asked for, not which image
    # answers, and it is resolved by this host's own daemon — the party a verifier
    # is checking.
    #
    # Built from main after the controller stack landed and pushed as :dev-amd64 on
    # 2026-08-14. Verified to contain it rather than assumed from the tag: the
    # binary carries 0g-controller, ATTEST_PROXY_SOCKET, the enc-key derivation and
    # the container-label invalidation, and `docker run <digest> 0g-controller`
    # starts the controller instead of reporting an unknown command.
    #
    # :dev-amd64 is a shared, moving tag — that is exactly why this line names the
    # digest instead. Re-resolve after every push, and update all five places
    # together (this image:, IMAGE_DIGEST below, and the same pair on the event and
    # controller services); they must be identical or the digest the broker
    # announces on-chain is not the one it is running:
    #
    #   docker buildx imagetools inspect ghcr.io/0gfoundation/0g-serving-broker:dev-amd64
    image: ghcr.io/0gfoundation/0g-serving-broker@sha256:ec5df8347f91c3b28a6638db4e24dba343799c0a3a7e2cdd44845a3a27f2e734
    ports:
      - "80:3080"
    environment:
      - PORT=3080
      - CONFIG_FILE=/etc/config/config.yaml
      # A literal, not ${TARGET_URL}: this is the value a verifier reads to learn where
      # the broker forwards a request after unsealing it, and only a literal is inside
      # what compose_hash covers. A reference would put it back in the encrypted-env
      # channel the config file already uses, which is measured nowhere.
      #
      # Takes precedence over service.targetUrl in the config file — see loadConfig.
      - TARGET_URL=http://0gm-sglang:8000/v1
      - NETWORK=phala
      # What this container reports on-chain as the image it runs. The controller
      # rewrites both whenever it recreates this container on a new digest, so the
      # pair moves with the image; a recreated container inherits the old
      # environment, and without them the broker would come up on the new image
      # still announcing the previous digest. Must match image: above.
      - IMAGE_REPO=ghcr.io/0gfoundation/0g-serving-broker
      - IMAGE_DIGEST=sha256:ec5df8347f91c3b28a6638db4e24dba343799c0a3a7e2cdd44845a3a27f2e734
      # Quotes, response signatures and the enclave encryption key all come from
      # the controller now, not from dstack directly. Setting this is only what
      # makes the two missing mounts below workable; the missing mounts are what
      # provide the property.
      - TEE_SOCKET=/var/run/zg-tee/tee.sock
    volumes:
      # Read-only, so the only writer of this file is the controller — which is
      # what makes zg-config-update a complete account of it rather than an audit
      # trail of one route among several.
      - broker-config:/etc/config:ro
      - ./logs/broker:/var/log/inference
      - ./logs/event:/var/log/event
      # Neither dstack's socket nor docker's. That is the point, and it is the only
      # part of this file that provides a property rather than describing one:
      #
      #   - dstack serves EmitEvent from the same unauthenticated handler as
      #     GetQuote and binds that socket 0777, so a container holding it can
      #     append to RTMR3 — including a record about the image it is itself
      #     running, which is what would make such a record unable to describe it.
      #   - it also serves GetKey, so a container holding it can derive the
      #     previous image's signing key and keep signing with it after an upgrade.
      #   - docker's socket lets a container stop, remove and recreate any other,
      #     which is what would make this file unable to say who may change what.
      #
      # Adding either back silently voids the attestation chain.
      - zg-tee:/var/run/zg-tee
    command: 0g-inference-server
    networks:
      - default
    healthcheck:
      test:
        [
          "CMD-SHELL",
          "test -L /proc/1/exe && readlink /proc/1/exe | grep -q broker",
        ]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s
    deploy:
      resources:
        reservations:
          devices:
            - driver: nvidia
              count: all
              capabilities: [gpu]
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      # With TEE_SOCKET set this container cannot finish starting until the
      # controller answers /SignerAddress, and it panics rather than falling back
      # to a local key. service_started (not service_healthy) and only in this
      # direction — the controller has no reverse dependency, so there is no cycle.
      # Without it the broker crash-loops until it happens to win the race.
      0g-controller:
        condition: service_started
      mysql:
        condition: service_healthy
      0gm-sglang:
        # Block broker from accepting traffic until SGLang passes /v1/models;
        # there is no LiteLLM in the middle, so a not-ready engine would
        # surface as 502s on /v1/messages.
        condition: service_healthy
      broker-config-init:
        # There is no config file at all until this has run, so this is a hard
        # prerequisite rather than an ordering preference.
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  # Event service starts after broker is ready
  0g-serving-provider-event:
    container_name: 0g-serving-provider-event
    image: ghcr.io/0gfoundation/0g-serving-broker@sha256:ec5df8347f91c3b28a6638db4e24dba343799c0a3a7e2cdd44845a3a27f2e734
    environment:
      - CONFIG_FILE=/etc/config/config.yaml
      # Same as the broker's. cmd/event picks its TEE client from this and falls
      # back to Phala when unset — right on this node, but only by accident, and
      # silently wrong the day this deployment moves to gcp or alicloud.
      - NETWORK=phala
      - IMAGE_REPO=ghcr.io/0gfoundation/0g-serving-broker
      - IMAGE_DIGEST=sha256:ec5df8347f91c3b28a6638db4e24dba343799c0a3a7e2cdd44845a3a27f2e734
      - TEE_SOCKET=/var/run/zg-tee/tee.sock
    volumes:
      - broker-config:/etc/config:ro
      - ./logs/event:/var/log/inference
      # Same reasoning as the broker: no dstack socket, quotes through the
      # controller. The controller upgrades this container alongside the broker,
      # so the two always run the same digest.
      - zg-tee:/var/run/zg-tee
    command: 0g-inference-event
    networks:
      - default
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "grep -q '0g-inference-event' /proc/1/cmdline"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    logging:
      driver: "json-file"
      options:
        max-size: "100m"
        max-file: "5"
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      0g-controller:
        condition: service_started
      0g-serving-provider-broker:
        condition: service_healthy

  # The only container that holds dstack's socket, and the only one that holds
  # docker's. It serves the broker and the event service GetQuote, Info, Sign,
  # SignerAddress and GetEncKey over zg-tee — and deliberately NOT GetKey, so a
  # broker image cannot derive a key it could keep across an upgrade.
  #
  # Its own image is pinned here and nowhere else: nothing measures the
  # controller, so this line is what a reviewer is trusting. Review this digest
  # with the same care as the broker's.
  0g-controller:
    container_name: 0g-controller
    # Published so an upgrade can be triggered without SSH into the CVM. Reachable
    # through the dstack gateway as <app-id>-3090.<gateway-domain> on 443.
    #
    # What guards it is the admin signature alone: AuthMiddleware requires an
    # EIP-191 signature by a controller.adminAddresses entry. controller.allowedIPs
    # does NOT help here — traffic arrives via the gateway, so the source address
    # the controller sees is the gateway's, not the caller's.
    #
    # And the admin key is provider-level control, not just an image switch:
    # PUT /v1/config/core takes the WHOLE config file and validates only that it is
    # YAML, and no baseline for that file is published anywhere
    # (see 0gfoundation/0g-router#728).
    # Until that is fixed, treat this key exactly like the SSH key it replaces, and
    # prefer terminating this at an ingress that can expose /v1/images/update alone.
    ports:
      - "3090:3090"
    image: ghcr.io/0gfoundation/0g-serving-broker@sha256:ec5df8347f91c3b28a6638db4e24dba343799c0a3a7e2cdd44845a3a27f2e734
    environment:
      - CONFIG_FILE=/etc/config/config.yaml
      # Where it serves the attestation proxy. Also the switch that makes
      # UpdateImages willing to record anything: with this unset the broker would
      # derive its own key at a fixed path and no record written here could ever
      # match a quote, so the controller refuses to upgrade at all.
      - ATTEST_PROXY_SOCKET=/var/run/zg-tee/tee.sock
    volumes:
      # Writable, unlike the broker's: the controller is the writer, and
      # ApplyCoreConfig rewrites this file after recording the change in RTMR3.
      #
      # A named volume, not /dstack/user_config, and not an inline compose config:
      # both of those are re-materialised from the deployment's copy whenever the
      # container is recreated, which would silently revert a change the controller
      # had already recorded in RTMR3 and leave the on-chain record describing a
      # file that no longer says that. broker-config-init writes into this volume
      # once and then leaves it alone.
      - broker-config:/etc/config
      - /var/run/dstack.sock:/var/run/dstack.sock
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - zg-tee:/var/run/zg-tee
      - ./logs/controller:/var/log/inference
    depends_on:
      # Without this the controller can start before its config exists, and a
      # missing config file is not an error to loadConfig — it returns defaults,
      # where controller.enable is false and adminAddresses is empty. The container
      # would look healthy while serving nothing, which is the whole deployment.
      broker-config-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    command: 0g-controller
    networks:
      - default
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "grep -q '0g-controller' /proc/1/cmdline"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    logging:
      driver: "json-file"
      options:
        max-size: "100m"
        max-file: "5"
    restart: unless-stopped

  prometheus-init:
    # Same digest as broker-config-init, so pinning costs nothing extra to maintain.
    # This one holds the ARMS credentials the rendered PROMETHEUS_CONFIG carries.
    image: alpine:3.18@sha256:de0eb0b3f2a47ba1eb89389859a9bd88b28e82f5826b6969ad604979713c2d4f
    environment:
      - PROMETHEUS_CONFIG=${PROMETHEUS_CONFIG:-}
    volumes:
      - prometheus-config:/tmp
    command: |
      sh -c 'if [ -n "$$PROMETHEUS_CONFIG" ]; then
        echo "$$PROMETHEUS_CONFIG" | base64 -d > /tmp/prometheus.yml
      else
        cat > /tmp/prometheus.yml << "EOF"
      global:
        scrape_interval: 15s
      scrape_configs:
        - job_name: "0g-serving"
          static_configs:
            - targets: ["0g-serving-provider-broker:3080", "0g-serving-provider-event:3081"]
        - job_name: "node-exporter"
          static_configs:
            - targets: ["prometheus-node-exporter:9100"]
      EOF
      fi'

  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:v2.45.2
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - prometheus-config:/etc/prometheus
    # No ports, same reason as mysql — and Prometheus has no authentication at
    # all, so publishing it served /api/v1/query to anyone. Grafana queries it
    # over the compose network; remote_write pushes out, nothing needs to reach in.
    networks:
      - default
    healthcheck:
      test:
        [
          "CMD",
          "wget",
          "--no-verbose",
          "--tries=1",
          "--spider",
          "http://localhost:9090/-/healthy",
        ]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    depends_on:
      prometheus-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana-oss:11.4.0
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - ./grafana/provisioning:/etc/grafana/provisioning
      - ./grafana/dashboards:/var/lib/grafana/dashboards
    # No ports. Published, this was admin/admin on the public internet by way of
    # the gateway. Reach it by forwarding the port over the phala CLI, or publish
    # it again only together with the gateway's restrict mode and a real password
    # in GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD.
    environment:
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD:-admin}
    networks:
      - default
    healthcheck:
      test:
        [
          "CMD-SHELL",
          "curl -f http://localhost:3000/api/health || wget -q --spider http://localhost:3000/api/health",
        ]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s
    depends_on:
      prometheus:
        condition: service_healthy

  prometheus-node-exporter:
    image: prom/node-exporter:v1.7.0
    restart: always
    volumes:
      - /proc:/host/proc:ro
      - /sys:/host/sys:ro
      - /:/rootfs:ro
    command:
      - "--path.procfs=/host/proc"
      - "--path.sysfs=/host/sys"
      - --collector.filesystem.ignored-mount-points
      - "^/(sys|proc|dev|host|etc|rootfs/var/lib/docker/containers|rootfs/var/lib/docker/overlay2|rootfs/run/docker/netns|rootfs/var/lib/docker/aufs)($$|/)"
    networks:
      - default
    privileged: true
    depends_on:
      prometheus:
        condition: service_healthy
    expose:
      - 9100

  # NVIDIA GPU metrics exporter. Scraped by prometheus at dcgm-exporter:9400.
  # Exposes GPU utilization, memory used, temperature, power, PCIe throughput.
  dcgm-exporter:
    image: nvcr.io/nvidia/k8s/dcgm-exporter:3.3.5-3.4.0-ubuntu22.04
    restart: unless-stopped
    runtime: nvidia
    environment:
      - NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all
      - DCGM_EXPORTER_NO_HOSTNAME=1
    cap_add:
      - SYS_ADMIN
    networks:
      - default
    expose:
      - 9400
    depends_on:
      prometheus:
        condition: service_healthy

volumes:
  broker-config:
  mysql-data:
  prometheus-config:
  cert-data:
  # Carries the controller's attestation socket. Exactly three services may mount
  # it: the controller that serves it, and the broker and event service that use
  # it. That socket signs any 32-byte hash under the running broker image's key,
  # so a fourth container mounting it could mint response proofs attributed to a
  # reviewed image — and nothing in RTMR3 would record that container's existence.
  zg-tee:

networks:
  default:
    name: 0g-serving-network
    external: false
pre_launch_script:
#!/bin/bash
echo "----------------------------------------------"
echo "Running Phala Cloud Pre-Launch Script v0.0.19"
echo "----------------------------------------------"
set -e

# Function: notify host

notify_host() {
    if command -v dstack-util >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        dstack-util notify-host -e "$1" -d "$2"
    else
        tdxctl notify-host -e "$1" -d "$2"
    fi
}

notify_host_hoot_info() {
    notify_host "boot.progress" "$1"
}

notify_host_hoot_error() {
    notify_host "boot.error" "$1"
}

# Function: Perform Docker cleanup
perform_cleanup() {
    echo "Pruning unused images"
    docker image prune -af
    echo "Pruning unused volumes"
    docker volume prune -f
    notify_host_hoot_info "docker cleanup completed"
}

# Function: Check Docker login status without exposing credentials
check_docker_login() {
    local registry="$1"

    # When registry is specified, check auth entry for that registry in Docker config
    if [[ -n "$registry" ]]; then
        local docker_config_path="${DOCKER_CONFIG:-$HOME/.docker}/config.json"
        if [[ -f "$docker_config_path" ]] && grep -q "$registry" "$docker_config_path"; then
            return 0
        else
            return 1
        fi
    fi

    # Fallback check when no explicit registry is provided
    if docker info 2>/dev/null | grep -q "Username"; then
        return 0
    else
        return 1
    fi
}

# Function: print the SHA256 fingerprint of every authorized key
#
# Output matches `ssh-keygen -lf` and the fingerprints GitHub and Phala Cloud
# display, so an operator can match the boot log against the account's key list.
# The guest image ships neither ssh-keygen nor a base64 applet (BusyBox has
# base32 only), so openssl does both the decode and the digest.
print_authorized_key_fingerprints() {
    local file="$1"
    if ! command -v openssl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "openssl not available; skipping SSH key fingerprints"
        return 0
    fi

    local key_type blob comment decoded_bytes fingerprint
    # `|| [[ -n "$key_type" ]]` keeps the final line when the file does not end
    # with a newline; read returns non-zero there but still fills the variables.
    while read -r key_type blob comment || [[ -n "$key_type" ]]; do
        if [[ -z "$blob" ]]; then
            continue
        fi
        # openssl exits 0 on undecodable input and emits nothing, which would
        # otherwise print the SHA256 of the empty string as a real fingerprint.
        decoded_bytes=$(printf '%s' "$blob" | openssl base64 -d -A 2>/dev/null | wc -c || true)
        if [[ "$decoded_bytes" -eq 0 ]]; then
            echo "  $key_type <unreadable key>"
            continue
        fi
        fingerprint=$(
            printf '%s' "$blob"                 | openssl base64 -d -A 2>/dev/null                 | openssl dgst -sha256 -binary 2>/dev/null                 | openssl base64 -A 2>/dev/null                 | tr -d '='                 || true
        )
        echo "  $key_type SHA256:$fingerprint"
    done < "$file"
}

# Main logic starts here
echo "Starting login process..."

# Check if Docker credentials exist
if [[ -n "$DSTACK_DOCKER_USERNAME" && -n "$DSTACK_DOCKER_PASSWORD" ]]; then
    echo "Docker credentials found"
    DOCKER_REGISTRY_TARGET="${DSTACK_DOCKER_REGISTRY:-docker.io}"
    echo "Target Docker registry: $DOCKER_REGISTRY_TARGET"

    # Check if already logged in
    if check_docker_login "$DSTACK_DOCKER_REGISTRY"; then
        echo "Already logged in to Docker registry: $DOCKER_REGISTRY_TARGET"
    else
        echo "Logging in to Docker registry: $DOCKER_REGISTRY_TARGET"
        # Login without exposing password in process list
        if [[ -n "$DSTACK_DOCKER_REGISTRY" ]]; then
            if ! echo "$DSTACK_DOCKER_PASSWORD" | docker login -u "$DSTACK_DOCKER_USERNAME" --password-stdin "$DSTACK_DOCKER_REGISTRY"; then
                echo "Docker login failed: $DOCKER_REGISTRY_TARGET"
                notify_host_hoot_error "docker login failed"
                exit 1
            fi
        elif ! echo "$DSTACK_DOCKER_PASSWORD" | docker login -u "$DSTACK_DOCKER_USERNAME" --password-stdin; then
            echo "Docker login failed: $DOCKER_REGISTRY_TARGET"
            notify_host_hoot_error "docker login failed"
            exit 1
        fi
        echo "Docker login successful: $DOCKER_REGISTRY_TARGET"
    fi
# Check if AWS ECR credentials exist
elif [[ -n "$DSTACK_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID" && -n "$DSTACK_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY" && -n "$DSTACK_AWS_REGION" && -n "$DSTACK_AWS_ECR_REGISTRY" ]]; then
    echo "AWS ECR credentials found"

    # Check if AWS CLI is installed
    if [ ! -f "./aws/dist/aws" ]; then
        notify_host_hoot_info "awscli not installed, installing..."
        echo "AWS CLI not installed, installing..."
        if ! curl "https://awscli.amazonaws.com/awscli-exe-linux-x86_64-2.24.14.zip" -o "awscliv2.zip"; then
            echo "AWS CLI download failed"
            notify_host_hoot_error "awscli install failed"
            exit 1
        fi
        if ! echo "6ff031a26df7daebbfa3ccddc9af1450 awscliv2.zip" | md5sum -c; then
            echo "MD5 checksum failed"
            notify_host_hoot_error "awscli install failed"
            exit 1
        fi
        unzip awscliv2.zip &> /dev/null
    else
        echo "AWS CLI is already installed: ./aws/dist/aws"
    fi

    # Set AWS credentials as environment variables
    export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="$DSTACK_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID"
    export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="$DSTACK_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"
    export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="$DSTACK_AWS_REGION"

    # Set session token if provided (for temporary credentials)
    if [[ -n "$DSTACK_AWS_SESSION_TOKEN" ]]; then
        echo "AWS session token found, using temporary credentials"
        export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="$DSTACK_AWS_SESSION_TOKEN"
    fi

    # Test AWS credentials before attempting ECR login
    echo "Testing AWS credentials..."
    if ! ./aws/dist/aws sts get-caller-identity &> /dev/null; then
        echo "AWS credentials test failed"
        # For session token credentials, this might be expected if they're expired
        # Log warning but don't fail startup
        if [[ -n "$DSTACK_AWS_SESSION_TOKEN" ]]; then
            echo "Warning: AWS temporary credentials may have expired, continuing startup"
            notify_host_hoot_info "AWS temporary credentials may have expired"
        else
            echo "AWS credentials test failed"
            notify_host_hoot_error "Invalid AWS credentials"
            exit 1
        fi
    else
        echo "Logging in to AWS ECR..."
        if ./aws/dist/aws ecr get-login-password --region "$DSTACK_AWS_REGION" | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin "$DSTACK_AWS_ECR_REGISTRY"; then
            echo "AWS ECR login successful"
            notify_host_hoot_info "AWS ECR login successful"
        else
            echo "AWS ECR login failed"
            # For session token credentials, don't fail startup if login fails
            if [[ -n "$DSTACK_AWS_SESSION_TOKEN" ]]; then
                echo "Warning: AWS ECR login failed with temporary credentials, continuing startup"
                notify_host_hoot_info "AWS ECR login failed with temporary credentials"
            else
                notify_host_hoot_error "AWS ECR login failed"
                exit 1
            fi
        fi
    fi
fi

perform_cleanup

#
# GHCR image pull access verification (pure HTTP, no docker daemon)
#
if [[ "$DOCKER_REGISTRY_TARGET" == "ghcr.io" && -n "$DSTACK_DOCKER_USERNAME" && -n "$DSTACK_DOCKER_PASSWORD" ]]; then
    COMPOSE_IMAGES=$(grep 'image:' /dstack/docker-compose.yaml 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $2}' | tr -d '"'"'" || true)
    HEADER="Accept: application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json,application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json,application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.list.v2+json,application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json"
    for img in $COMPOSE_IMAGES; do
        [[ "$img" != ghcr.io/* ]] && continue
        ref="${img#ghcr.io/}"
        # Digest-pinned refs (repo@sha256:...) use the digest as the manifest
        # reference; tag refs (repo:tag) use the tag, defaulting to latest.
        if [[ "$ref" == *@* ]]; then
            repo="${ref%%@*}"
            reference="${ref#*@}"
        else
            repo="${ref%%:*}"
            reference="${ref##*:}"
            [[ "$reference" == "$ref" ]] && reference="latest"
        fi
        echo "Verifying GHCR pull access: $img"
        token=$(curl -sf -u "$DSTACK_DOCKER_USERNAME:$DSTACK_DOCKER_PASSWORD" "https://ghcr.io/token?service=ghcr.io&scope=repository:${repo}:pull" | jq -r '.token // empty' || true)
        if [[ -z "$token" ]]; then
            echo "ERROR: GHCR token exchange failed for $img"
            notify_host_hoot_error "GHCR token exchange failed: $img"
            exit 1
        fi
        http_code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Authorization: Bearer $token" -H "$HEADER" "https://ghcr.io/v2/${repo}/manifests/${reference}")
        if [[ "$http_code" != "200" ]]; then
            echo "ERROR: GHCR pull access denied for $img (HTTP $http_code)"
            notify_host_hoot_error "GHCR pull access denied: $img (HTTP $http_code)"
            exit 1
        fi
        echo "GHCR pull access OK: $img"
    done
fi

#
# Pull latest images from docker-compose.yaml so existing CVMs pick up new tags.
# Pull is fail-soft: short-lived tokens may expire between login and pull, but
# falling back to already-cached images is preferable to blocking boot.
#
echo "Images before pull:"
docker images --format '{{.Repository}}:{{.Tag}} {{.ID}} ({{.CreatedSince}})'

echo "Pulling latest images from /dstack/docker-compose.yaml..."
if docker compose -f /dstack/docker-compose.yaml pull; then
    echo "docker compose pull completed"
    notify_host_hoot_info "docker compose pull completed"
else
    echo "WARNING: docker compose pull failed; continuing with existing images"
    notify_host_hoot_info "docker compose pull failed; using existing images"
fi

echo "Images after pull:"
docker images --format '{{.Repository}}:{{.Tag}} {{.ID}} ({{.CreatedSince}})'

#
# Set root password.
#
echo "Setting root password.."

# Check if password files are writable
PASSWD_WRITABLE=true
if [ ! -w /etc/passwd ]; then
    echo "Warning: /etc/passwd is read-only"
    PASSWD_WRITABLE=false
fi
if [ ! -w /etc/shadow ]; then
    echo "Warning: /etc/shadow is read-only"
    PASSWD_WRITABLE=false
fi

if [ "$PASSWD_WRITABLE" = "false" ]; then
    echo "Skipping password setup due to read-only file system"
else
    # Check if chpasswd is available
    if command -v chpasswd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "Using chpasswd method"

        if [ -n "$DSTACK_ROOT_PASSWORD" ]; then
            echo "Setting root password from user.."
            echo "root:$DSTACK_ROOT_PASSWORD" | chpasswd
            unset DSTACK_ROOT_PASSWORD
            echo "Root password set/updated from DSTACK_ROOT_PASSWORD"
        elif [ -z "$(grep '^root:' /etc/shadow 2>/dev/null | cut -d: -f2)" ]; then
            echo "Setting random root password.."
            # dstack guest busybox lacks head -c (FANCY_HEAD off); dd is the
            # last pipeline command, so its 0 status masks tr's SIGPIPE exit.
            DSTACK_ROOT_PASSWORD=$(
                LC_ALL=C tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' < /dev/urandom | dd bs=1 count=32 2>/dev/null
            )
            echo "root:$DSTACK_ROOT_PASSWORD" | chpasswd
            unset DSTACK_ROOT_PASSWORD
            echo "Root password set (random auto-init)"
        else
            echo "Root password already set; no changes."
        fi
    else
        # No chpasswd: do not pipe into interactive passwd(1). It often reads
        # /dev/tty and fails with "password for root is unchanged" during boot.
        echo "Using passwd method"

        if [ -n "$DSTACK_ROOT_PASSWORD" ]; then
            echo "Setting root password from user.."
            if command -v passwd >/dev/null 2>&1 && passwd --help 2>&1 | grep -q -- '--stdin'; then
                echo "$DSTACK_ROOT_PASSWORD" | passwd --stdin root
            elif command -v openssl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                # busybox passwd has no --stdin; write the SHA-512 crypt hash
                # into /etc/shadow directly instead of driving interactive passwd.
                HASHED_ROOT_PASSWORD=$(openssl passwd -6 "$DSTACK_ROOT_PASSWORD")
                sed -i "s|^root:[^:]*:|root:${HASHED_ROOT_PASSWORD}:|" /etc/shadow
                unset HASHED_ROOT_PASSWORD
            else
                echo "Error: cannot set DSTACK_ROOT_PASSWORD non-interactively"
                echo "Need chpasswd, passwd --stdin, or openssl"
                exit 1
            fi
            unset DSTACK_ROOT_PASSWORD
            echo "Root password set/updated from DSTACK_ROOT_PASSWORD"
        elif [ -z "$(grep '^root:' /etc/shadow 2>/dev/null | cut -d: -f2)" ]; then
            # Never lock the account here: sshd built without PAM (dstack dev
            # images) treats a locked account as "deny all authentication",
            # which breaks public-key SSH too. Set a discarded random password
            # by writing its crypt hash into /etc/shadow directly.
            if command -v openssl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "Setting random root password.."
                DSTACK_ROOT_PASSWORD=$(
                    LC_ALL=C tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' < /dev/urandom | dd bs=1 count=32 2>/dev/null
                )
                HASHED_ROOT_PASSWORD=$(openssl passwd -6 "$DSTACK_ROOT_PASSWORD")
                sed -i "s|^root:[^:]*:|root:${HASHED_ROOT_PASSWORD}:|" /etc/shadow
                unset DSTACK_ROOT_PASSWORD HASHED_ROOT_PASSWORD
                echo "Root password set (random auto-init)"
            else
                echo "Warning: no openssl to hash a random password; leaving root password empty"
            fi
        else
            echo "Root password already set; no changes."
        fi
    fi
fi

#
# Set SSH authorized keys
#
if mkdir -p /home/root/.ssh 2>/dev/null; then
    if [[ -n "$DSTACK_ROOT_PUBLIC_KEY" ]]; then
        echo "$DSTACK_ROOT_PUBLIC_KEY" > /home/root/.ssh/authorized_keys
        unset DSTACK_ROOT_PUBLIC_KEY
        echo "Root public key set"
    fi
    if [[ -n "$DSTACK_AUTHORIZED_KEYS" ]]; then
        echo "$DSTACK_AUTHORIZED_KEYS" > /home/root/.ssh/authorized_keys
        unset DSTACK_AUTHORIZED_KEYS
        echo "Root authorized_keys set"
    fi

    if [[ -f /dstack/user_config ]] && jq empty /dstack/user_config 2>/dev/null; then
        if [[ $(jq 'has("ssh_authorized_keys")' /dstack/user_config 2>/dev/null) == "true" ]]; then
            # jq -r terminates the value with a newline; jq -j does not, which
            # both concatenated the next appended key onto the same line and
            # made line-based counting report one key fewer than the file holds.
            jq -r '.ssh_authorized_keys' /dstack/user_config >> /home/root/.ssh/authorized_keys
            # Drop duplicates and the blank line an empty key list produces.
            sort -u /home/root/.ssh/authorized_keys > /home/root/.ssh/authorized_keys.tmp
            mv /home/root/.ssh/authorized_keys.tmp /home/root/.ssh/authorized_keys
            KEY_COUNT=$(grep -c '^[^[:space:]]' /home/root/.ssh/authorized_keys || true)
            echo "Set root authorized_keys from user preferences, total $KEY_COUNT keys"
            print_authorized_key_fingerprints /home/root/.ssh/authorized_keys
        fi
    fi
else
    echo "Warning: Cannot create /home/root/.ssh directory (read-only file system?)"
    echo "Skipping SSH key setup"
fi

if [[ -S /var/run/dstack.sock ]]; then
    export DSTACK_APP_ID=$(curl -s --unix-socket /var/run/dstack.sock http://dstack/Info | jq -j .app_id)
elif [[ -S /var/run/tappd.sock ]]; then
    export DSTACK_APP_ID=$(curl -s --unix-socket /var/run/tappd.sock http://dstack/prpc/Tappd.Info | jq -j .app_id)
fi
# Check if DSTACK_GATEWAY_DOMAIN is not set, try to get it from user_config or app-compose.json
# Priority: user_config > app-compose.json
if [[ -z "$DSTACK_GATEWAY_DOMAIN" ]]; then
    # First try to get from /dstack/user_config if it exists and is valid JSON
    if [[ -f /dstack/user_config ]] && jq empty /dstack/user_config 2>/dev/null; then
        if [[ $(jq 'has("default_gateway_domain")' /dstack/user_config 2>/dev/null) == "true" ]]; then
            export DSTACK_GATEWAY_DOMAIN=$(jq -j '.default_gateway_domain' /dstack/user_config)
        fi
    fi

    # If still not set, try to get from app-compose.json
    if [[ -z "$DSTACK_GATEWAY_DOMAIN" ]] && [[ $(jq 'has("default_gateway_domain")' app-compose.json) == "true" ]]; then
        export DSTACK_GATEWAY_DOMAIN=$(jq -j '.default_gateway_domain' app-compose.json)
    fi
fi
if [[ -n "$DSTACK_GATEWAY_DOMAIN" ]]; then
    export DSTACK_APP_DOMAIN=$DSTACK_APP_ID"."$DSTACK_GATEWAY_DOMAIN
fi

echo "----------------------------------------------"
echo "Script execution completed"
echo "----------------------------------------------"
